datasets.title: U.S. inventor ages, gender and death dates matched to patents
datasets.description: Author-built database matching U.S.-resident patent inventors to estimated birth years, inferred gender and some death dates collected from public web directories, linked to patents by inventor ID.

Use only for legitimate research, follow your institution's data-ethics rules, and do not use it to identify or contact individuals.

Quality caveats from the authors: ages come from heuristics and a quality score; death dates are described as less reliable. The checked age file has birth years from 1800 to 2013, so apply plausibility filters.

Twenty-three public files, 3 MB to 1.9 GB. The key files are the inventor age and gender table (2,408,326 rows; 1,858,516 unique inventors), a patent-to-inventor crosswalk (8,080,135 rows, grant years 1976 to 2018) and a death-date table. Other files were listed but not read.
Gender is inferred from first name and birth year by an algorithm; 571,074 rows are marked unknown.
The Dataverse record is marked CC0 1.0. Source websites for the scraped information may have their own terms.
A companion data paper (Kaltenberg, Jaffe and Lachman, “The Age of Invention”, NBER working paper 28768) documents the database.

datasets.title: U.S. patent secrecy orders in World War II
datasets.description: Author-compiled list of U.S. patent applications placed under secrecy orders in the Second World War era, with filing dates, serial numbers and, where granted, patent numbers for linking to other patent data.
notes: One data table (8,475 secrecy-order records) and a README. 6,353 records have a patent number and grant date; the rest were not matched to a granted patent.
The table has five columns: filing date, serial number, secrecy determination, patent number and grant date. All rows carry the same determination value, 'Secrecy Recommended'.
Compiled from War Department and Office of Scientific Research and Development records held at the U.S. National Archives; the README gives the finding aids.
Licensed CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial). The README asks users to cite the paper. Patent numbers link to USPTO data such as PatentsView, which is already listed.

datasets.title: Inventors, firms and patent output (replication archive)
datasets.description: Author replication archive linking U.S. patents and inventors to publicly listed firms, with citation measures, inventor employment spells, firm financial variables, Stata code and bootstrap results.
notes: 25 public files, about 2.9 GB. The largest is the inventor-patent file at 1.9 GB. Includes Stata code (a master script runs the analysis in order), MATLAB files and a README listing every variable.

The README says some source files, for example full Compustat data, cannot be shared publicly. The archive contains Compustat-derived files; the authors' record says the files and code replicate the paper's results, but check which inputs are partial before assuming a full rebuild.
Personal data: the LinkedIn match file (23,703 rows) contains inventor names with employer names and employment dates. Handle in line with research ethics rules.
Underlying patent data derive from the NBER patent files (already listed). Compustat terms may restrict reuse of the financial variables. The repository labels the record CC-BY-4.0.
Bootstrapped results may not replicate exactly because of random resampling, according to the authors.
datasets.verification: DataverseNL API lists 25 public files under CC-BY-4.0 (version 1.0, August 2025; the original Erasmus repository DOI forwards here). The README was read in full. datasets.title: Panel Study of Entrepreneurial Dynamics (PSED)
datasets.description: Longitudinal surveys that follow nationally representative samples of people starting businesses in the United States, with data on start-up activities, resources, networks and whether the venture emerges.
notes: Two cohorts: PSED I (screening 1998-2000, 830 nascent entrepreneurs, three follow-ups) and PSED II (screening 2005-2006, six yearly interviews), plus harmonized outcome files that combine them, according to the project site.

The PSED project site states that the data, including restricted geographic data, are distributed through ICPSR. ICPSR downloads need a free account; the restricted geographic data have extra conditions.

The cited papers state in their abstracts that they use PSED I, PSED II or the harmonized files. One cited paper is a replication study of PSED-based work and reports that only some replications succeeded; treat results from this survey with that in mind.
Not verified: ICPSR blocks scripted access, so the data files themselves were not opened for this entry. The ICPSR studies were confirmed through their DOI records, not by download.

Some papers use that restricted version, for example a Management Science paper on minority-owned start-ups and a Review of Financial Studies paper on capital structure. They are not cited here because they did not use the public files.
The cited papers state in their abstracts that they use the Kauffman Firm Survey but do not say whether it was the public-use or the restricted version. Check before comparing results.
The Stata public-use file name has dashes; SAS users must remove them, according to the foundation's page.

datasets.title: Reliance on Science — patent-to-paper citations
datasets.description: Author-released data linking patents to the scientific articles they cite, with confidence scores and whether the reference is on the front page or in the text, plus patent-paper pairs.
notes: The Zenodo concept DOI points to the latest of 64 versions. The two latest releases hold only U.S. patents, according to the record, 'in contrast to earlier releases'. The SMJ article studies worldwide front-page citations, so its data correspond to older versions; those were not inspected and the version used in the paper is not verified.

Latest release files: the citation table (1.44 GB; columns include reference type, confidence score, an article identifier named oaid, patent number and where the reference was found), a patent-paper-pairs table (59,202 rows: article id, patent id, confidence level) and a PDF describing the pairs.

Licensed CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial); the authors ask to be contacted about commercial use. The record asks users to cite the SMJ article, a Journal of Economics and Management Strategy article and a patent-paper-pairs paper.
Citation counts and linking rely on automated extraction and matching, so errors remain; the confidence score helps filter.
datasets.verification: Zenodo API lists three open files in the latest release under CC BY-NC 4.0. The pairs table was downloaded and parsed (59,202 rows, 3 columns). The first rows of the citation table were read by range request. Earlier versions were listed (64 in all) but not opened.

datasets.title: Defense SBIR/STTR awards linked to patents and commercialization
datasets.description: Author-built database linking U.S. Department of Defense small business research awards to the utility patents they produced and to web pages that signal commercialization.
notes: Covers Department of Defense SBIR and STTR awards only, not other agencies. Award data come from the Defense Contract Action Data System (1984-2001) and USAspending.gov (2001-2018); patent data mainly from PatentsView, with details from the Patent Examination Research Dataset or PATSTAT; web pages were collected by the authors' crawls.
Ten small tables (under 5 MB each), including awards (2,213 rows), patents (42,342), award-to-patent links (3,623), web pages (2,027) and legal entities (9,902), plus a README and a schema diagram.
Version 1.1 (August 2025). The record lists the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 license and a copyright notice for the authors. The web page table holds addresses and dates, not page content.
This is a derived research database, not the official SBIR.gov award files.
datasets.verification: Zenodo API lists 12 open files. Five tables and the README were downloaded and parsed (row counts above). The remaining tables were listed, not read.

datasets.title: Disruptiveness (CD index) of U.S. patents — replication data
datasets.description: Author replication data with patent-level disruptiveness (CD index) values for U.S. utility patents under several measurement choices, with citation counts, technology field and an R script.
notes: Patent-level files for granted U.S. utility patents from 1976 to 2016 in several variants (with and without citation-window truncation, and adjusted for application dates), each as CSV and as R fst files; the largest CSV is 770 MB. Small summary tables and the replication R script are included.
The record states that the R script replicates all figures and tables of the paper. The script and the large files were not run.
Licensed CC BY 4.0. The underlying patent and citation data are public U.S. patent records.
A separate library entry covers other patent measures; this one is the disruptiveness measure only.

datasets.verification: Zenodo API lists 29 open files under CC BY 4.0. datasets.title: Firms in technological space (topological analysis) — replication package
datasets.description: Author replication package with firm-level patent counts by technology area and year, the code to map firms in technology space, and regression data combining the map statistics with firm financial variables.
notes: Includes 30 yearly CSV files of R&D, M&A and combined patent counts by firm and technology area, Python code for the topological (Mapper) analysis, Stata regression code and the data for the main regressions, a README and the draft paper with its online appendix.

Patent data are the first author's compilation of USPTO patents granted 1976-2010, combined with Securities Data Company merger data. Firm financial variables from Compustat (1976-2005) enter only in the regression file; the authors state they have permission to publish their derived outputs, but Compustat is a licensed source, so check its terms.
Licensed CC BY 4.0; the Python code is also on the author's GitHub page under GPL-3.0 according to the README.
Runtime for the main outputs is under 10 minutes on a desktop according to the README. Nothing was run for this entry.

links.title: Python code and patent count files (ZIP, 23 MB)

datasets.verification: Zenodo API lists five open files in version 1.1 under CC BY 4.0. The README was downloaded and read and the code archive was downloaded and listed (322 entries, including yearly distance tables). The Stata archive and the draft paper were not opened.

datasets.title: Entrepreneurs' social vision statements on AngelList (study 1 data)
datasets.description: Author-shared data for one of two studies: coded statements by start-ups on a talent platform about their social vision and the number of job applications received, with R scripts for both studies.
notes: Only part of the paper's data is public. Study 1 (a table of 1,191 start-up profiles with 66 columns, including coded statements and number of applications) and the R scripts are downloadable. The Study 2 field-experiment data file is marked restricted in the repository and was not accessed.
Company names and platform profile links appear in the study 1 table; they come from public start-up profiles but may be sensitive in publications.
Licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0: non-commercial and no derivatives. Version 1.1.
The record describes the two studies' datasets as XLSX files, one per study, plus scripts for descriptives and analyses and a folder of custom functions.
datasets.verification: DataverseNL API lists nine files, eight public and the Study 2 data restricted. The study 1 workbook was downloaded and parsed (1,191 rows, 66 columns). The R scripts were listed, not run.

datasets.title: Mannheim Innovation Panel (MIP), German innovation survey
datasets.description: Annual representative survey of the innovation activities of German firms (new products and processes, innovation spending, returns), the German part of the Community Innovation Surveys, available to researchers as anonymised scientific use files.
notes: Not freely downloadable. The ZEW Research Data Centre offers on-site use, time-limited remote access, an anonymised scientific use file for non-commercial research and, for some MIP data, an education use file. Scientific use is limited to researchers at publicly funded research institutions, according to ZEW and the DataCite record's rights statement.

The survey has run annually since 1993 and is a panel of firms in mining, manufacturing, energy, construction and business-related and distribution services, according to the DataCite description. The scientific use files in the DOI records cover 1993 to 2016 (one earlier release 1993 to 2014).

The eight Research Policy papers cited are those the data provider's own DOI records list as documenting publications; which version of the MIP data each paper used (scientific use, on-site or earlier releases) is not stated in the record. Their full texts were not read.
Not verified: no data file was opened. ZEW's pages and DOI records were checked; the files need an application to the ZEW Research Data Centre.
datasets.verification: ZEW's MIP page and Research Data Centre page were read and confirm the annual survey since 1993, scientific use files and the access routes. DataCite records for the scientific use files give the restriction wording and list the documenting publications. No data file could be inspected.

datasets.title: Democracy and innovation: country panel (replication data)
datasets.description: Author replication data with a country-year panel of democracy measures, patenting and control variables used to test whether democratization raises innovation.
notes: Four Stata data tables and a do-file: the main panel has 10,914 country-year rows for 214 countries from 1960 to 2010 (31 variables), plus a patent-based table of 357 rows and supplementary versions. A README maps each file to the paper's tables.
The Dataverse record is marked CC0 1.0. The source of each variable was not checked for this entry; see the README and the paper.
Files were read but the analysis was not rerun.
datasets.verification: Dataverse API lists six public files under CC0 1.0 (version 1.0). All were downloaded; the four Stata tables parsed (10,914, 357, 10,914 and 392 rows) and the README was read.

datasets.title: U.S. cleantech startups and their alliances (panel)
datasets.description: Author-built panel of U.S. cleantech startups and their alliances with governments, firms, research organisations and not-for-profits, with startup outcomes, and the Stata code for the paper.
notes: The paper describes 657 U.S. cleantech startups and 2,015 alliances from 2008 to 2012. The deposited panel table has 2,408 rows and 24 columns with 657 distinct startup identifiers; a Stata do-file reproduces the regressions.
Licensed CC BY-NC 3.0 (non-commercial) on Mendeley Data. The table has no text columns: startups are identified by number only.
The deposit has only the panel table and a Stata do-file; there is no separate codebook, so variable meanings come from the paper and the do-file. All 24 columns are numeric.
datasets.verification: Mendeley Data lists two public files. Both were downloaded (sizes match the declared sizes); the panel table parsed to 2,408 rows and 24 columns with 657 distinct identifiers over 2008 to 2012, and the do-file was read.

datasets.title: Lithium-ion battery core patent families
datasets.description: Author-compiled list of the roughly 420 patent families on the core knowledge trajectory of lithium-ion battery technology, from a patent citation network analysis, with family details and network indices.
notes: One Excel sheet with 419 patent-family rows and 50 columns (network index, patent family identifier, filing and publication dates, grant status, country, family size and more). Earliest filing dates run from 1970 to 2015 in the file.
The paper analyses 101,620 patent families from 1970 to 2018; this deposit holds only the identified core trajectory, not the full set.
Licensed CC BY-NC 3.0 on Mendeley Data (non-commercial). Patent identifiers are DOCDB family IDs (column docdb_family_id).
datasets.verification: Mendeley Data lists one public file. It was downloaded (size matches the declared size) and parsed with 419 patent rows and 50 columns.

datasets.title: Government ideology and innovation: country panel
datasets.description: Author-shared country-year panel combining measures of government ideology with patent and trademark applications, R&D spending and macroeconomic controls.
notes: One Excel sheet with 1,573 rows and 73 columns covering 102 countries from 1995 to 2015 in the file. The paper states 110 countries, so the deposit may be a subset or an earlier version.

The column headings are in Chinese (for example country name, year, R&D spending as a share of GDP, resident and non-resident patent and trademark applications) with some indicator names in English in the format used by World Bank data (for example GDP per capita (constant 2010 US$)). The original sources of the variables were not checked.
Licensed CC BY 4.0 on Mendeley Data. The deposit's own description just says 'see detailed in data file'; there is no separate codebook.
datasets.verification: Mendeley Data lists one public file. It was downloaded (size matches the declared size) and parsed with 1,573 rows, 73 columns, 102 countries and years 1995 to 2015.

datasets.title: Expert survey ratings versus official research spending (replication data)
datasets.description: Author replication data comparing World Economic Forum survey ratings of business research spending, and education outcomes, with official spending figures and income across countries.
notes: Two Stata country-year tables for the regressions (research spending: 1,078 rows across 138 countries, 2006 to 2017; education outcomes: 252 rows) and three CSV tables for the figures, plus a replication code file.

The paper's abstract says the ratings are World Economic Forum survey assessments compared with official spending figures; the abstract does not name the source of the official figures. Check the underlying sources' own terms for reuse.
Licensed CC BY 4.0 on Mendeley Data.
datasets.verification: Mendeley Data lists six public files. All were downloaded (sizes match the declared sizes); the tables parsed with the row counts above, and the replication code file was downloaded.

datasets.title: Emerging market categories and incumbent innovation (author data)
datasets.description: Author-shared main dataset for a study of how the number of emerging market categories in an industry relates to incumbent firms' innovation efforts.
notes: One Stata table of 72,778 rows and 73 columns whose column names suggest four-digit industry (SIC) measures and counts of publications, awards and meetings. The deposit says only 'main dataset used to test our hypotheses'; there is no codebook or code, so the variables are hard to interpret without the paper.
Licensed CC BY 4.0 on Mendeley Data (released after an embargo). The unit of observation and the years are not stated in the deposit.
Treat as a data release without documentation: read the paper's methods section before use.
